$comment: THE app's data layer. Declare entities here and the backend engine materializes SQLAlchemy models AND a full REST API per entity at startup — no models.py or CRUD routes to write, ever. Generated per entity: GET /api/<plural> (equality filters on any field, ?q= search across string/text/enum fields, range filters <field>_gte/_lte/_gt/_lt, plus orderBy=<field>&order=asc|desc&limit&offset), POST /api/<plural>, POST /api/<plural>/bulk (JSON array, one transaction), GET/PUT/DELETE /api/<plural>/{id}, GET /api/<plural>/_stats?groupBy=&agg=count|sum|avg&field=, and GET /api/_meta/schema. Every entity automatically gets: integer autoincrement 'id', 'createdAt'/'updatedAt' ISO timestamps, camelCase JSON on the wire (snake_case in the DB — the engine converts). Field types: string (255 chars), text, integer, float, boolean, datetime (ISO-8601 strings on the wire), json, enum (add "values": ["a","b"] — validated, union-typed in types.gen.ts), ref (holds the integer id of another entity; add "entity": "Name"; deleting a parent CASCADES children whose ref is required, NULLs optional refs — override with "onDelete"). Add "unique": true to any scalar field (duplicates -> 409). Field spec keys: type (required), required, default, unique, values (enum), entity (ref), onDelete (ref). Entity spec keys: description, fields, plural. Do NOT declare id/createdAt/updatedAt — they are automatic. Writing this file also regenerates frontend/types.gen.ts + schema.gen.ts (typed entities + the metadata powering <EntityForm>/<EntityTable>). The CLI's data commands (livingui <project> select/insert/update/delete) work against these tables immediately.
